title: Assessment of quality of commercial hand sanitizers using FTIR and gas chromatography
author: Alam, Rahat, et al.

steps.title: Prepare FTIR calibration standards
steps.instruction: Dilute each absolute alcohol (ethanol, IPA, methanol) with water to obtain mixtures of 100/0, 80/20, 70/30, 60/40, and 50/50 (v/v). Load 20–30 µL of each mixture into a calcium‑fluoride capillary sample holder and place on the FTIR window. Record spectra from 4000 to 400 cm⁻¹, scanning each standard at least three times (n = 3).

steps.title: Scan hand sanitizer samples (FTIR)
steps.instruction: Load 20–30 µL of each commercial sanitizer into a calcium‑fluoride capillary, place on the FTIR window, and record spectra under the same conditions (4000–400 cm⁻¹, three scans per sample). Export the raw data, edit in Excel to regenerate the spectra, and calculate the average peak heights for the relevant vibrational modes.

steps.title: Validate IR calibration curves
steps.instruction: For each alcohol, compute the standard deviation, relative standard deviation, and linear‑range correlation coefficient (R²) from the three peak‑height measurements. Accept a calibration curve only if R² > 0.905. Construct the curves using the average peak heights of the designated vibrational modes (see Table 1).

steps.title: Build ethanol calibration curves
steps.instruction: Using the ethanol standards with water contents 0, 20, 30, 40, 50 % (corresponding to the 100/0‑50/50 mixtures), record the peak heights of the C‑H stretching band (~2975 cm⁻¹) and the C‑H bending band (881 cm⁻¹). Plot height versus ethanol concentration and calculate R² values (0.905 for C‑H stretching, 0.980 for C‑H bending).

steps.title: Build IPA calibration curves
steps.instruction: Prepare IPA standards with water percentages 0, 30, 40, 50, 60 %. Record peak heights of the C‑H stretching band (~2970 cm⁻¹) and the CH₃‑C‑CH₃ bending band (952 cm⁻¹). Generate calibration plots and obtain R² = 0.913 for C‑H stretching and R² = 0.922 for CH₃‑C‑CH₃ bending.

steps.title: Attempt IPA C‑O calibration (optional)
steps.instruction: Construct a calibration curve for IPA using the C‑O stretching band; note that the resulting R² is < 0.700, indicating poor linearity, so this curve is not used for quantification.

steps.title: Build methanol calibration curves
steps.instruction: Prepare methanol standards with water contents 0, 20, 30, 40 %. Measure peak heights of the C‑H stretching band (~2943 cm⁻¹) and the C‑O stretching band (1032 cm⁻¹). Plot the data and calculate R² = 0.904 for C‑H stretching and R² = 0.996 for C‑O stretching.

steps.title: Prepare GC‑FID calibration standards and samples
steps.instruction: Make working standard solutions of ethanol, IPA, and methanol at several concentrations in toluene. Dilute each hand‑sanitizer sample 25‑fold with toluene. Inject exactly 0.01 µL of each standard or diluted sample with the auto‑injector onto the GC column (SCION‑5, 30 m × 0.25 mm, 0.25 µm film) operating at a carrier‑gas flow of 1.5 mL/min. Perform each injection in triplicate (n = 3).

steps.title: Quantify ethanol by FTIR
steps.instruction: Apply the accepted ethanol calibration curves (C‑O, C‑H stretching, C‑H bending) to the average peak heights obtained from each sanitizer spectrum to calculate ethanol concentration; compare the results with label values and GC measurements.

steps.title: Quantify IPA by FTIR
steps.instruction: Use the IPA C‑H stretching and CH₃‑C‑CH₃ bending calibration curves to convert the measured peak heights of each sanitizer into IPA concentration; verify the values against GC results.

steps.title: Quantify methanol by FTIR
steps.instruction: Employ the methanol C‑H and C‑O stretching calibration curves to determine methanol content in each sanitizer from the recorded peak heights; compare with GC data.

description: Alcohol content, standard deviation (SD), relative standard deviation (RSD) and linear range correlation coefficient (R2) were measured to validate the IR spectroscopy as an analytical method [24]. For each standard curve, at least three peak heights (n = 3) were used, and the generated curve was taken into account if the square correlation coefficients (R2) were greater than 0.905. The calibration curves were constructed using the average peak heights of the relevant alcohol's vibrational modes. Figures S7(a), (b) and (c) show the IR spectra of pure ethanol, IPA and methanol, respectively. As seen from Figures S7(a), (b) and (c), red and blue circles indicate C−H and C−O stretching and the purple circle shows C-H bending while green and orange circles represent −C(CH3)2 bending and C−C−O symmetric stretching, respectively [18]. In this study, these functional groups were considered in order to detect and quantify the different alcohols in alcohol-based commercial hand sanitizers.
